turns.assessment: The affected services converge on lightpath och4, and errored seconds were recorded at both och4 line interfaces, while services on the S15–S04 portion remained healthy. Unchanged power, OSNR, BER, DGD, SOP-rate, and amplifier telemetry strongly argue against a persistent amplifier, span-loss, WSS attenuation, or hard line-card fault. A very brief polarization/mechanical transient on the S04–S14 route best fits the sparse errored seconds and protection switching, but there is no evidence localizing it to a particular span or direction, so no repair target reaches 80% confidence.

proposals.rationale: A sub-second polarization transient on the signal arriving at the S04 end of och4 could produce errored seconds without appearing in sampled optical telemetry.
A transient on the signal arriving at the S14 end provides the same fit. The data do not identify which span or direction was responsible.
Brief handling of a span could cause the event, although the absence of a recorded power excursion makes a primarily polarization-driven transient more likely.
The reverse direction is equally unlocalized; no power-monitor change identifies a particular span.
Receiver-local degradation could cause errors at S04 with a normal optical path, but it does not explain the errored seconds at both line ends well.
Receiver-local degradation at S14 remains possible but similarly fails to explain the bidirectional evidence.
An OTN-layer interruption could leave optical telemetry unchanged, but a switch-fabric failure should interrupt every ODU through S04, conflicting with the many healthy services.

score.why: truth not in the reported set
